messages.author: 54ff474bd99c96ba
messages.subject: RE: is SEM possible with this number of indicators
parts:
I am trying to perform SEM however am a complete newbie to this and not even sure my data is appropriate for the analysis - I am mainly concerned I don't have enough indicators for the analysis to work. My model is pasted below and would really appreciate if anyone could confirm whether theoretically this should work or not?

# model:

model_full <- '

# Measurement

  control =~ Q33 + Q24 + Q519 + Q520 + Q521

  trust =~ Q517 + Q522

  affect =~ Q543 + Q526

  costs =~ Q14 + Q16 + Q27 + Q523 + Q525 + Q518

  bene =~ Q13 + Q15

  tolerance =~ Q17

# Regressions

  costs ~ control + trust + affect

  bene ~ trust + affect + costs

  tolerance ~ costs + affect + bene

 

# Residual Correlations

 

'

messages.author: 08146071976f553f
messages.subject: Re: is SEM possible with this number of indicators
parts:
Hello Rebecca,

As a rule of thumb: there are at least 3 indicators in 1-factor model and at least 2 indicators in multifactor models. Soo for instance your tolerance factor has only 1 indicator which is too low. I would prefer to use at least 3 indicators per factor to be safe
Looks like you might run into problems because of that, and of course you will need a substantial sample size

cheers,

Guido

messages.author: 5b9c62b1c7cbc1e6
messages.subject: Re: is SEM possible with this number of indicators
parts:
Rebecca,

Sample size in SEM is always a bit of guesswork, unless you have really good information about likely parameter estimates. In the absence of simulations tailored to your problem, though, my practical experience is 1,500 is probably ample for a model of this size.

Also, I think, but wouldn't swear to it, that the defaults imposed by sem() and cfa(), though probably not lavaan(), will make the adjustments needed for your single-indicator factor. Though it will behave statistically like an observed variable, and probably not have any benefit over using 'Q17' directly in the regressions without setting up 'tolerance'.

Pat
